_doc: The arsenal's tools (winning-build plan 2026-11-13, sections 3.3-3.5, slice 5). Brandon: a kid should 'identify and learn about monsters, then strategically find a way to exploit the weakness... throwing potions, targeting weaknesses, sacrificing defense for damage based on monster... elemental attacks and status attacks both ways'. Read by src/coatings.py (coatings and thrown flasks, data/items/flask.json), src/stance.py (Press or Guard, the two-hander's parry) and src/counters.py (named counters). Every number here is real base data, never scaled by the floor (LORE NOT FLOOR).

coating._doc: A coating (a flask's 'coat' block in data/items/flask.json) goes on the weapon in the hero's hand for one turn and no question, as a potion is drunk. Its substance joins the weapon's own (combat._substances_of), so it meets a weakness through the one bane rule: silver dust on a steel mace hits a werewolf as silver. It is worth the weak step against a creature that cannot bear it and never makes a blow weaker. Each blow that lands spends one; the last says so. A rider (venom's poison, frost's slowing, fire's burning) takes hold only on a creature that does not resist or shrug off the substance and whose nature allows the effect (status_immune). 'aliases': other items that are the same thing (the holy water foraged at an altar coats and throws as a Flask of Holy Water does).
coating.applied: You work the {coat} into your {weapon}. It is {word} for the next {blows} blows that land.
coating.replaced: The {old} on your {weapon} is scraped away for the {coat}.
coating.worn_off: The last of the {coat} wears off your {weapon}.
coating.no_weapon: You have no weapon in your hand to coat.
coating.ranged: A coating is for a blade or a head that strikes, not a bow.
coating.already: Your {weapon} is already {word}: the {coat} would add nothing.
coating.card_weapon: Coated with {coat}: {word} for {blows} more blows that land.
coating.card_coat: Coats the weapon in your hand: {word} for {blows} blows that land (Shift+C or Apply).
coating.card_rider: Each blow may leave it {effect} for {turns} turns.
coating.card_rider_sure: Each blow leaves it {effect} for {turns} turns.
coating.card_throw_weak: Thrown: {damage} holy damage to the unholy; only water to anything else.
coating.card_throw_status: It leaves its target {effect} for {turns} turns.

throw._doc: A flask's 'throw' block: real damage of its type through Monster.take_damage (weak x2, resisted x0.5, shrugged off x0.25: data/affinity_rules.json), sized so a flask on a weak kind is about one chain of a common weapon at the flask's own depth (floor_curve.ONE_ATTACK at its peak floor, halved for the weak step, written in the data). 'only_weak': holy water harms only the unholy. 'status': what the splash leaves (burning, an acid-pitted hide), if the creature does not resist the type. Fire still frightens what fears fire (affinity_rules fear_of_fire).
throw.only_water: The {flask} splashes {the}. It is only water to {him}.

stance._doc: Press or Guard (plan 3.4, decision 7): one key (Shift+S) steps through Neutral, Press and Guard, and takes one turn, as swapping a weapon does: chosen for the fight, not for each blow. 'damage' multiplies every weapon blow and shot (combat.strike_damage); 'ac' is armour points gained (Guard) or given up (Press) in Player.get_ac. Neutral by default; kept in the save.

neutral.name: Neutral
neutral.line: You settle into an even stance.

press.name: Press
press.line: You set your feet and press the attack: harder blows, and an open guard. (+30% damage, 2 AC worse)

guard.name: Guard
guard.line: You tuck in behind your weapon and give ground only on your terms. (-30% damage, 2 AC better)

parry._doc: A two-handed melee weapon wielded with no shield turns blows aside (plan 3.4: a deep hero without a shield was hit about 95% of the time; half a par shield). AC from its template, else its class for a named weapon with no template; plus 'tier_bonus' by the weapon's tier (its material's, or a unique's own). Read by Player.get_ac through stance.parry_ac; shown on the weapon card. Never from the floor.
parry.card: Parry +{ac}: two hands on the haft turn blows aside (no shield).

counters._doc: Named counters (plan 3.3): an item's 'counters' list (a shield template's, an accessory's) names techniques it blocks outright while worn, or while carried where the technique says 'carried'. 'gaze': a gaze attack does nothing at all (no damage, no rider), from Medusa's to a floating eye's. 'voice': the rider of a voice attack (a wail's fear, a song's sleep, a scream's confusion) never takes hold; the price is that the hero hears nothing while the wax is in ('deafens': no war-band heard on arriving, no growl from a pet that smells what he cannot see). 'fey_glamour': the charm, confusion, sleep and visions of the Fair Folk slide off (the same rule as a cold-iron body armour's ward, data/gear_rules.json wards). 'apply': the Kit's Apply action toggles a counter that is put in or taken out (the earplugs), one turn either way.

gaze.name: a gaze
gaze.line: You watch {the} in the bright face of your {item}, and the gaze slides off.
gaze.card: Mirror-bright: a gaze slides off it, harmless (no damage, no paralysis, nothing).

voice.name: a voice
voice.line: {The}'s voice cannot get past the wax in your ears.
voice.card: Put in (Apply), no voice can work on you: no wail's fear, no song's sleep, no scream's confusion. But you hear nothing while they are in.

fey_glamour.name: fey glamour
fey_glamour.line: The cold iron you carry bites, and the glamour of {the} falls away.
fey_glamour.card: Carried, the Fair Folk's glamour slides off you: no fairy charm, confusion, sleep or visions.

stop_ears.in: You knead the wax soft and press it into your ears. The world goes quiet, as it did for Odysseus's crew.
stop_ears.out: You pull the wax from your ears. The dungeon's noises rush back in.
stop_ears.unheard: Your ears are stopped: you hear nothing of what is on this floor.
